2. Facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the petitioners in this writ petition impugned the purported cancellation of the mutation of the names of the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 relating to Mutation Case No. 13610 of 04 and 16962 of 04 by the respondent No. 5 Assistant Commissioner (Land) Savar, Dhaka, pursuant to a purported report of the respondent No.3 Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka in respect of 2.99 acres of land at CS Khatian Nos. 11 and 12, CS and SA Dag No.2, 23 and 86 of Mouza-Purbo Narshinghapur, Police Station-Ashulia, formerly Savar, Dhaka. It is stated that petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 purchased a total of 2.99 acres land from petitioner No.1. The said properties were purchased by the petitioner No.2 by registered Deed No. 13426 dated 30-4-2004 and the petitioner No.3 by registered Deed No. 13427 dated 30-6- 2004 which were duly mutated in the names of the said petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 being Mutation Case No. 13610 of 2004 and 16962 of 2004. It is alleged that the impugned order of cancellation has been done behind the back of the petitioners. In other words, the impugned order of cancellation was passed by the respondents upon an investigation alleged to have been done beyond the knowledge of the petitioners. 

 3. When the petitioners came to know about the impugned cancellation and purported investigation, the petitioner No. 2 went to collect the copy of the same order respectively on 9-7-2007 and 12-7-2007 from the respondent Nos. 3 and 5, but was refused by them. Thereafter, an application for the certified copy of the impugned order was made which was also refused. It is also stated that even respondent No.5 refused to receive the application of the petitioner for obtaining certified copy. Having failed to get the order, the petitioner No.2 requested the respondent for showing him the cancellation order so that he could take note of it in his hand which was also refused. Thereafter, the petitioners sent a notice demanding justice on 12-7-2007 requesting for the cancellation of the impugned investigation report and the cancellation order and supplying a copy of the said order which was not even responded to and, as such, they being aggrieved, moved this Division under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing with Mr Md Asaduzzaman, Advocate on behalf of the petitioners, after taking us through the impugned order and different Annexures appended to the petition, at the very outset has made out a clear submission that the impugned order of cancellation was done behind the back of the petitioners pursuant to a purported investigation which was absolutely beyond their knowledge. Therefore, the learned Counsel by placing reliance on two decisions namely, Faridsons Ltd vs Government of Pakistan reported in 13 DLR (SC) 233 and Nawabkhan Abbaskhan vs State of Gujrat reported in AIR 1974 (SC) 1471 mooted out the age old maxim audi alteram partem on the circumstances as stated above and argued that without giving any opportunity of hearing the impugned order of cancellation passed by the respondent which cannot be sustained under law. He further brought to our notice that the petitioner No.2 came to know about the purported investigation conducted by respondent No.3 and filed an application on 9-7- 2007 before the respondent No.2 for reinvestigation and he marked the file to the respondent No. 4 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka which is still pending and the impugned order came during the pendency of that application which is an absolutely arbitrary exercise of power by the respondents. 

 5. He also stated in the pennon that the following civil cases are pending before the several Courts between the parties: 

 8. The process of cancellation of mutation has been done as per law. Next, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that several civil cases in different Courts including the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh are pending for determination of title and possession of the proper- ties including the properties in question between the parties and, on that score, this writ petition is not maintainable. She placed reliance on the decision of Shahajadi Begum Waqf Estate vs Secretary, Ministry of Communication (Roads and Railway) Dhaka, Bangladesh reported in 2001 BLD (AD) 59 = 7 BLC (AD) 41 on the point. 

 12. Chapter 6 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, governs the procedure relating to mutation proceeding. In particular, Rules 22 to 24 deal with the proceeding to be adopted in the mutation case. Any grievance on the decision of the Revenue Officer in this respect can be well ventilated by an appeal under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. It is found that the petitioners instead of preferring an appeal, which they should have done on receiving the order of cancellation on 12-7-2007 in the normal course of events, preferred this writ petition. We also find that without preferring appeal on the same date i.e. on 12-7-2007, they served notice demanding justice. This is absolutely bereft of the approved procedure as laid down in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act under section 147 and the Tenancy Rules 1955, (22 to 24 and 31).
